# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot
digraph process {
    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
        "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer subagent asks questions?";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
    "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];

    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/superpowers/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns

    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
```

func IsCondensableEndedSession(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) bool {

```bash
go build ./... && go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/ -count=1 2>&1 | tail -3

## Strengths

- **Plan fidelity is exact.** `sessionSweepNeeded`, `maybeSpawnSessionSweep`, the test, and the lifecycle comment match Task 5's spec verbatim, and all four Task-3 polish items landed correctly: the `lerr != nil` re-load branch now Debug-logs with session ID, the "mirror this in the PR description" parenthetical is gone, the vanished-branch sentence got the "in practice" softening, and the ENDED-only pre-filter comment in `runSessionSweep`'s loop was added (`/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/claude-hooks/cmd/entire/cli/session_sweep.go:98-102`).
- **The pure/impure split is the right design.** `SpawnDetached` no-ops under `go test` (`testing.Testing()` guard in `execx/spawn_detached.go`), so putting all decision logic in a pure `sessionSweepNeeded(states, now)` is the only way to make "would we spawn?" testable. The test's doc comment names exactly this rationale.
- **Failure isolation is genuinely airtight.** `maybeSpawnSessionSweep` returns void; both error paths bail (one logged, one silent); `SpawnDetached` swallows every internal error by contract and detaches with `context.Background()` so the child never inherits hook cancellation. No git object reads, no locks, no network on this path — nothing here can propagate an error or block into `handleLifecycleSessionStart`'s return.
- **Hook-latency claim holds up.** The cost is one `os.ReadDir` of `.git/entire-sessions/` plus a JSON decode per state file (`session/state.go:737`), plus one `proclive.Check` per ACTIVE state — hostname + bootID + a single `procStat` probe (`proclive.go:159`), the same per-state cost `entire status` already pays. `paths.WorktreeRoot` is cached. The only expensive thing, the fork, happens exactly when a zombie exists. This is sub-millisecond-per-state work; the comment's "small shared-directory read" claim is honest.
- **Placement last in the handler is right.** It runs after the banner write (so hook-visible output is never delayed behind the sweep decision) and after the `MutateSessionState`/`EventSessionStart` transition (so the decision sees the freshest state for the current session). A best-effort void call as the final statement before `return nil` is the correct shape.
- **File coherence is intact.** `session_sweep.go` reads top-to-bottom as one story: threshold constant → predicate → detached runner → spawn decision → spawn site. All four functions share the predicate; nothing else has leaked in.
- **Spawn-storm behavior matches the plan's fence honestly.** N concurrent session starts → N detached sweeps, serialized by per-session locks; losers re-load and see `FullyCondensed`/cleared state and no-op. A persistently failing zombie re-spawns on every session start, and `runSessionSweep`'s contract says so plainly ("a failed session is logged and retried by the next sweep"). That is the accepted design per the plan's out-of-scope section, not an accident.

## Issues

**Critical:** none.

**Important:** none.

**Minor:**

1. **Asymmetric error swallowing in `maybeSpawnSessionSweep`** (`session_sweep.go:163-166`). The `ListSessionStates` failure gets a Debug log, but the `paths.WorktreeRoot` failure is a bare `return`. If that ever fails persistently, "zombie detected but sweep never spawns" becomes invisible even at DEBUG. One symmetric `logging.Debug` line would close the gap. Cosmetic — the branch is nearly unreachable inside a hook that already resolved the root earlier in the same handler.

2. **The repeated-spawn acceptance lives only in `runSessionSweep`'s doc.** The spawn site's comment covers latency and best-effort, but not "a zombie that persistently fails to condense re-nominates a spawn on every session start — accepted, no debounce by design." A future reader hitting repeated "zombie session detected, spawning detached sweep" Info lines in logs will look at `maybeSpawnSessionSweep` first; half a line there (or in the lifecycle.go comment) would mark it as chosen rather than overlooked. The plan's out-of-scope fence says exactly this — it just isn't quoted at the place where the storm originates.

3. **A resumed zombie flags its own SessionStart — undocumented direction of the race.** `captureSessionOwner` runs only at TurnStart (`manual_commit_hooks.go:2427`), so when a user resumes a session whose previous agent died, at SessionStart the state is still ACTIVE with the dead owner fingerprint. `sessionSweepNeeded` will (correctly) flag it and the sweep may finalize the session that is in the middle of being resumed. The outcome is coherent — `finalizeExitedSessions` re-validates under the per-session lock, the finalize is lossless, and the resumed session's first TurnStart re-establishes state — and `entire status`/doctor already carry the identical race. But the safety-contract comment discusses only the ENDED→ACTIVE resume direction; a sentence covering the ACTIVE-dead-owner-being-resumed case would make the contract complete. Observation, not a fix request.

4. **Duplicate directory scan per session start.** `CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints` earlier in the same handler already lists session states; `maybeSpawnSessionSweep` re-lists. At this cost (one ReadDir + a few JSON decodes) threading the list across the strategy/cli boundary would buy coupling, not speed — I'd leave it as is; noting only so nobody "optimizes" it into a shared snapshot that then feeds the sweep stale data.

5. **Test scope is minimal but adequate.** `TestSessionSweepNeeded` covers nil/healthy/mixed exactly per plan; it doesn't exercise the ACTIVE-dead-owner nomination through `sessionSweepNeeded`, but that path is fully covered by `TestIsSweepableZombie` and the wrapper is a trivial any-loop. No action needed.

**Approved.** Task 5 is implemented exactly to plan, all four review polish items landed, the hot-path cost analysis in the comments is honest and verified against the actual code, failure isolation is complete, and the accepted spawn-storm behavior matches the plan's explicit fence. - **Plan fidelity is exact.** `sessionSweepNeeded`, `maybeSpawnSessionSweep`, the test, and the lifecycle comment match Task 5's spec verbatim, and all four Task-3 polish items landed correctly: the `lerr != nil` re-load branch now Debug-logs with session ID, the "mirror this in the PR description" parenthetical is gone, the vanished-branch sentence got the "in practice" softening, and the ENDED-only pre-filter comment in `runSessionSweep`'s loop was added (`/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/claude-hooks/cmd/entire/cli/session_sweep.go:98-102`).

gh pr create --title "feat: self-heal zombie sessions via detached sweep from session-start" --body "## Problem

Zombie sessions linger until a human runs \`entire doctor\`: (a) ACTIVE sessions whose agent process died without a stop hook are only finalized when someone happens to run \`status\`/\`doctor\`; (b) ENDED sessions holding uncondensed checkpoint data wait for a commit in their context that may never come — a real one sat stuck for 4 days with 60 checkpoints until a manual \`doctor --force\`, slowing every commit in the meantime (the O(N) ended-session scan PostCommit pays).

## Design

- **Detection (cheap, hook-side):** at the end of the session-start hook, \`maybeSpawnSessionSweep\` lists the shared session-state files and runs a pure predicate (\`isSweepableZombie\`) — one state-dir read plus the same per-ACTIVE-state liveness probe \`entire status\` already pays. No repo access on the hot path.
- **Trigger:** if any zombie exists, fire-and-forget \`execx.SpawnDetached(root, \"__sweep_sessions\")\` (hidden infra command, \`__send_analytics\`/\`__refresh_trail_enablement\` pattern, with the sibling's file-logging bootstrap so diagnostics land in \`.entire/logs/\` instead of the discarded stdio). The hook's timeout budget is untouched regardless of backlog.
- **The sweep** reuses the existing engines, adding none: \`finalizeExitedSessions\` for ACTIVE-dead-owner (re-validated under the per-session lock), and \`CondenseSessionByID\` — the same engine \`doctor --force\` uses — for ENDED zombies, gated by a **24h age threshold** (younger ended sessions keep their PostCommit carry-forward chance; that skip in \`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed\` is deliberate design) and by \`strategy.IsCondensableEndedSession\` (newly exported; shadow branch must still exist).

## Safety contract, honestly stated

- **Condense-only**: sessions with steps but no shadow branch are doctor's *discard* case and are never touched automatically. This is enforced by the sweep's pre-checks (re-load + full re-predicate immediately before acting), not by the engine — if the shadow branch vanishes inside the seconds-wide window before the engine's lock, the engine clears the state, which in practice only happens when a concurrent condense already succeeded.
- **Residual races (narrowed, not closed):** a session resumed (ENDED→ACTIVE) in the instant between re-check and engine lock still gets condensed — acceptable against a >24h-idle precondition, and coherent (new turns re-accumulate). The reverse direction (ACTIVE-dead-owner being resumed mid-sweep) is safe because finalize re-validates under the lock and owner capture happens at TurnStart.
- **Spawn storms accepted by design:** N concurrent session-starts spawn N sweeps; per-session locks make the losers idempotent no-ops. A zombie that persistently fails to condense re-spawns on every session-start (logged, retried) — no global lockfile/debounce, per the plan's scope fence.
- **Known boundaries:** an IDLE session with a dead owner is out of scope (matches \`finalizeExitedSessions\`/doctor's existing boundary — \`OwnerExited\` is ACTIVE-only). Pre-existing and adjacent: \`StateStore.Load\` purges sessions older than 7 days, so the sweep's effective window for a persistently-failing zombie is 24h–7d; after that the stale purge (not the sweep) removes it — unchanged by this PR, which strictly improves the outcome inside the window.

## Tests

TDD throughout (each failing run verified before implementing): \`TestIsSweepableZombie\` (9-case table incl. the PID-reuse dead-owner fixture and the carry-forward age gate), \`TestRunSessionSweep_CondensesOldEndedZombie_LeavesFreshAlone\` (mutation-checked during review: fails if the age gate or fresh-session protection regresses), \`TestSessionSweepNeeded\` (pure spawn decision — \`SpawnDetached\` no-ops under \`go test\` by design). Full \`mise run fmt && mise run lint && go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...\` green; every commit builds standalone.

## Docs

\`docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md\` gained a Background zombie sweep paragraph; CLAUDE.md's hidden-commands list now includes \`__sweep_sessions\`.

Investigated 2026-08-17. `a9a676e79` (Aug 14) removed local_dev hook mode; `scripts/entire-dev` no longer exists on main. Three lingering effects on Peyton's machine:

1. **UserPromptSubmit 30s timeouts**: 68 of 139 worktrees under `.worktrees/` (plus the main checkout, whose local `main` is 345 commits behind) still have the pre-removal `.claude/settings.json` committed, routing hooks through `scripts/entire-dev` (go build from source per prompt; cold cache ≈27.6s measured). Claude Code's default UserPromptSubmit timeout is 30s. Fix is taking latest main in that worktree, NOT raising the hook timeout.
2. **git push blocked from updated worktrees — FIXED 2026-08-17**: shared `.git/hooks/pre-push` still ran `./scripts/entire-dev` with no `|| true` → exit 127 → push rejected. Repaired via `go run ./cmd/entire doctor --force` from the claude-hooks worktree (hooks are repo-shared, so this fixed pushes for all worktrees). Same run condensed stuck session 7aaa3b08 (Aug 13, 60 checkpoints → checkpoint 01M08E6EF7XB2RGAVV69EN0YXB). Still open from that scan: 4 Codex hooks await trust approval (open /hooks inside Codex).
3. **Self-repair not yet shipped in a release**: `72759d952` ("feat(doctor): check and repair stale git hooks", adds `GitHooksOutdated` + EnsureSetup reinstall on TurnStart) merged to main AFTER the Aug-15 nightly cut; installed `0.10.1-nightly.202608150610.7ddf2fc26` lacks it and as of Aug 17 no newer nightly exists. Irrelevant for this repo now (hooks manually repaired) but other repos with legacy hooks need a newer nightly. A prior session's report wrongly claimed the Aug-15 nightly contained the repair. Side find: doctor's stuck-session prompt crashed without a TTY (`huh: bubbletea: could not open TTY`) instead of degrading — fixed in PR #2015 (branch fix/doctor-stuck-session-no-tty, off main in the claude-hooks worktree): guard with CanPromptInteractively, print `--force` hint, TDD'd via TestRunSessionsFix_NonInteractive_HintsForceInsteadOfPrompting.

content.text:
Done — **PR #2029**: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2029

The full pipeline ran as planned: 6 tasks, each implemented by a fresh subagent under TDD, each passing a spec-compliance review and a code-quality review (with real fixes forced along the way), then a final whole-branch review that independently re-verified the safety claims against the code and re-ran the complete fmt/lint/test gate before declaring it ready.

**What shipped** (7 commits on `feat/zombie-session-sweep`):
- `isSweepableZombie` predicate + `sessionSweepNeeded` — the cheap hook-side decision (24h age gate protecting PostCommit carry-forward).
- `runSessionSweep` — the background pass reusing the existing engines: `finalizeExitedSessions` for dead-owner ACTIVE sessions, `CondenseSessionByID` (doctor's engine) for old ENDED zombies, condense-only with re-load-and-re-check before acting.
- Hidden `__sweep_sessions` command with file-logging bootstrap, spawned detached from the session-start hook — zero hook-latency impact.
- Docs in `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and CLAUDE.md.

**What the reviews caught that the plan missed:** a test fixture that couldn't detect a dead owner, an overclaimed safety guarantee (rewritten as an honest residual-race contract), the detached child discarding all its own diagnostics (fixed with the sibling command's logging bootstrap), and the 7-day stale-purge interaction now documented as a known boundary in the PR body.

**Net effect on the original problem:** the Aug-13-style zombie that sat for 4 days now gets condensed automatically within moments of the next session starting in the repo — no doctor, no agent, no warning needed. Both PRs (#2015 doctor fix, #2029 sweep) are up and awaiting your review.
